co_deep_end_the.blurb: The Deep End is a short section of the Pool Wall, a cliff just north of Ouray. It sits to the right of the Wading Pool, with the old Two Kids Mine as the easy landmark. Nearly all of the sixteen lines are bolted, with just two traditional cracks, and the grades sit squarely in the harder middle of the sport scale: a couple at 5.10, a dozen between 5.11 and 5.12, and a few at 5.13. Shade covers the wall in the morning and sun arrives in the afternoon, so it suits warm-weather mornings. It is a good stop for climbers who already lead 5.11 and want steady, steep sport pitches close to town.

co_bermuda_triangle.blurb: Bermuda Triangle is one of the busier faces on the Dark Side, the shady hillside above Ophir between Telluride and Norwood, at roughly 9,700 feet. Eighteen routes, mostly traditional with a handful of bolted lines, cover the steep end of the scale: about a third at 5.10, then a spread through 5.11 and 5.12, with a few 5.13s. The rock is clean and splitter-like in places, and the face stays cool, which helps on hot summer days. Expect a short, steep trail to the base and a crag that rewards solid crack and sport leaders rather than beginners.
co_bermuda_triangle.approach: From the Dark Side's main trail along the water pipe, keep going past the Wild Westerlies turnoff to the next cairned trail on the right, which climbs steeply to the base of the wall.

co_turkey_rock_2.blurb: Turkey Rock is the biggest formation in the Upper Boulderfield area on Independence Pass, perched on the hillside west of the boulderfield above 10,000 feet. Most of the sixteen routes are traditional, with a few bolted lines, and several are two or three pitches long. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.8 range, where much of the climbing sits, up to a handful of 5.12s and one 5.13. The altitude keeps temperatures cool, which makes it a good escape on hot days. It faces south and west, and the base is a short uphill hike from the road.
